transcript:
[doctor] Good morning, Mr. Smith. How are you doing today?

[patient] Good morning, doctor. I’ve been better, honestly.

[doctor] I see. I understand you’re here because of several concerns. Can you tell me more about what’s been going on?

[patient] Sure. Over the last six months, I’ve been feeling really fatigued and just overall low energy. My libido has decreased, and it’s been affecting my relationship. I also feel like I’m losing muscle mass and gaining fat, no matter what I do.

[doctor] Hmm, that sounds quite challenging. Have these symptoms been constant, or do they come and go?

[patient] They’re pretty much constant. Every day feels like a struggle, and it’s affecting my work and personal life.

[doctor] I’m sorry to hear that. You mentioned decreased libido. Are you also experiencing any difficulties with erections?

[patient] Yes, that’s been a problem too. It’s really frustrating.

[doctor] I can imagine. And you’ve noticed a reduction in muscle mass and an increase in body fat?

[patient] Yes, exactly. I used to be more muscular, but now I feel like I’m just getting softer.

[doctor] Have you had any issues with your mood or motivation lately?

[patient] Definitely. I’ve been feeling quite depressed and unmotivated. It’s hard to get out of bed some days.

[doctor] I’m sorry to hear that. It sounds like this has been very tough for you. Have you and your partner been trying to conceive?

[patient] Yes, we’ve been trying for a while now, but nothing’s happening. It’s really stressing us out.

[doctor] I see. Have you noticed any changes in the size of your testicles?

[patient] Yes, they seem smaller than they used to be.

[doctor] Thank you for sharing all of this. It gives me a good overview of what you’ve been experiencing. 

[patient] Sure, no problem.

[doctor] Can you tell me a bit about your medical history? Any previous diagnoses or chronic conditions?

[patient] No significant medical history. I just take a multivitamin daily.

[doctor] Okay, and any family history of medical conditions?

[patient] My father has Type 2 diabetes, and my mother has hypothyroidism.

[doctor] Got it. Any allergies?

[patient] None.

[doctor] How’s your sleep been?

[patient] Not great. I get about 6 hours a night, but it’s poor quality sleep.

[doctor] Okay. What about your diet?

[patient] I try to eat a balanced diet, but my appetite has been reduced lately.

[doctor] And exercise?

[patient] It’s inconsistent. I used to be more active, but now I’m mostly sedentary because of how I feel.

[doctor] Understood. Do you smoke or use tobacco?

[patient] No, I don’t smoke.

[doctor] How about alcohol?

[patient] Occasionally, maybe 1-2 drinks per week.

[doctor] Any drug use?

[patient] No.

[doctor] Alright. Do you engage in any recreational activities?

[patient] Not much lately. My symptoms have really limited my ability to do so.

[doctor] Thank you for that information. Let me take a look at your vital signs and perform a physical examination now.

[patient] Sure.

[doctor] Your blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg, and your pulse is 72 bpm. Your BMI is 27, which is in the overweight range. Let’s take a look at your general physical condition. You appear cooperative and in no acute distress. Now I’m going to examine your genital area.

[patient] Okay.

[doctor] Your external genitalia appear normal, but I do notice a decrease in testicular size. 

[patient] Is that bad?

[doctor] It can be a sign of underlying issues, but we’ll need some further tests to understand more. I’m going to order some blood tests to check your hormone levels, including testosterone, FSH, LH, prolactin, and estradiol. We’ll also check your complete blood count and Vitamin D levels.

[patient] Okay, sounds good.

[doctor] Additionally, I’m going to order a scrotal ultrasound to assess your testicular size and check for any abnormalities.

[patient] Alright. What do you think might be causing all of this?

[doctor] Based on your symptoms and physical examination, it’s possible that you have testicular hypofunction, which means your testicles might not be producing enough hormones like testosterone.

[patient] Oh, I see.

[doctor] We’ll have a clearer picture once we get the test results back. If it is testicular hypofunction, we can treat it. I’m considering starting you on testosterone replacement therapy. This would involve applying a 50 mg transdermal gel once daily.

[patient] Will that help with my symptoms?

[doctor] It should help address your symptoms like decreased libido, fatigue, and muscle mass reduction. It can also improve your mood.

[patient] That sounds promising.

[doctor] Alongside the medication, I recommend making some lifestyle changes. Regular physical activity, better sleep hygiene, and maintaining a balanced diet can significantly help.

[patient] I’ll try my best.

[doctor] I also recommend seeing a therapist to help manage the depressive symptoms you’ve been experiencing.

[patient] Okay, I think that would be helpful.

[doctor] We’ll follow up in about three months to see how you’re responding to the therapy and to monitor for any side effects. If the infertility issues persist, we might consider referring you to a fertility specialist.

[patient] That makes sense. Thank you, doctor.

[doctor] You’re welcome. We’ll get started on these tests and treatments, and hopefully, you’ll start feeling better soon.

[patient] I appreciate it.

[doctor] Take care, and I’ll see you in three months for your follow-up.

[patient] Thanks, doctor. See you then.
